history.summary: AMBIGUITY FLAG - THIS ENTRY IS THE LOCAL DWARKADHISH TEMPLE IN JAMNAGAR CITY (Kishan Park Society / Digvijay Plot area, near Bedi Gate), NOT the world-famous Dwarkadhish (Jagat Mandir) Temple at Dwarka in Devbhumi Dwarka district. Almost all web sources conflate the two: TripAdvisor and directory listings for the 'Dwarkadhish Temple, Jamnagar' address carry photos and reviews of the famous Dwarka temple (72 pillars, Chalukya-style reconstruction, five-storey shikhara on the Gomti creek, flag changed five times daily, 2,500-year tradition traced to Vajranabha, Krishna's great-grandson). The local Jamnagar temple - a Krishna (Dwarkadhish) shrine at Kishan Park Society, about 1.2 km from Jamnagar railway station - is listed on Google/JustDial with 4.5-5.0 ratings but no published history, deity details beyond Krishna, or founding date could be verified. If the CSV row intended the famous Dwarka temple, this file's coordinates, hours and history must be replaced.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple, Jamnagar
town_description: Jamnagar is a coastal city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kutch, founded in 1540 by Jam Rawal of the Jadeja Rajput clan as Nawanagar. Nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many temples, it is a major pilgrim and tourist hub whose landmarks include Lakhota Lake, the Lakhota Palace museum and the Bala Hanuman temple. The city is also an industrial centre, home to one of the world's largest oil refining complexes at nearby Motikhavdi.

travel.railway: Jamnagar railway station, about 1.21 km away (per yappe.in).
travel.road: Kishan Park Society, Digvijay Plot / Bedi Gate area; reachable by auto-rickshaw and city buses.
